primitives.name: Spot Status Lattice Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Spot status-only updates may repeat the price timestamp with `is_carried_forward=True`; do not deduplicate by timestamp alone.
primitives.assumptions: Timestamps are unique within a session unless explicitly marked as carried forward.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When `is_carried_forward=True`, the update does not constitute a new event but preserves prior state.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a partially ordered set of status events under temporal precedence, where carried-forward entries are equivalent elements in the poset.
layer2.telemetry: Event stream integrity check via duplicate detection logic.

primitives.name: Snapshot Status Inheritance Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Older unstated spot frames retain the last stated snapshot status.
primitives.assumptions: Unstated frames inherit the most recent known status until overridden.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In absence of explicit status change, previous status is propagated forward.

layer2.mapping: Derives a causal kernel that propagates status through time using inheritance rules rather than direct observation.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of status continuity across frame boundaries.

primitives.name: TWAP Status Evolution Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Snapshots carry status at batch level and may retain an older closing price; TWAP status changes with a new price.
primitives.assumptions: TWAP status depends directly on incoming price data, not on snapshot timing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Status transitions occur only upon receipt of a new price, regardless of snapshot frequency.

layer2.mapping: Models TWAP status as a dynamic function evolving with each price input, capturing temporal dependency without reliance on batch boundaries.
layer2.telemetry: Monitoring of TWAP status changes against price updates.

Snapshot inheritance ensures continuity of state even when no explicit update occurs, forming a robust baseline for inference. TWAP evolution introduces a functional dependency on price inputs, decoupling status from snapshot cadence. These operators together enable GSI to model market dynamics as a hybrid discrete-continuous system, where discrete events (price changes) trigger continuous state transitions (status updates). Failure modes include misinterpretation of carried-forward signals leading to incorrect state propagation, or ignoring snapshot staleness causing outdated status assertions.
